cvar_cost_map — DRIVE roverslip op

• Data kinds: image2d × scalar × any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.cvar_cost_map(dtm, cell: 'float', model, alpha: 'float' = 0.9, speed: 'float' = 0.05, s_max: 'float' = 0.9, soil_map=None, extrapolate: 'bool' = False) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import roverslip; roverslip.cvar_cost_map(dtm, cell: 'float', model, alpha: 'float' = 0.9, speed: 'float' = 0.05, s_max: 'float' = 0.9, soil_map=None, extrapolate: 'bool' = False) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("cvar_cost_map"))

Usage

From a digital terrain model (DTM), builds the travel time [s] of each 8-neighbor edge, discounted by the CVaR_α of the slip at the edge's slope (signed by the direction of travel).

dtm (H, W) [m], cell [m]. For edge (i, j) → neighbour k, slope θ = atan2(Δz, 水平距離), pessimistic slip ρ = CVaR_α(s(θ)) (θ ≥ 0) / CVaR_α(−s(θ)) (θ < 0), travel time L / (v (1 − ρ)), L being the 3-D edge length. ρ ≥ s_max and out-of-range are inf. With extrapolate = False (default), edges with slopes outside the angle range of the data the model was fitted to (x_range) are also inf (do not traverse slopes we do not know) —— a Gaussian process reverts to the prior mean outside the data, so if allowed to extrapolate it answers "no slip" the steeper the slope (the gate's trap). alpha = 0 gives the mean slip (risk-neutral). model is a single one, or a list of K paired with soil_map (H, W integers 0..K−1). Return value {"cost": (8, H, W), "risk_slip": (8, H, W), "pitch": (8, H, W) [deg], "offsets": (8, 2), "worst_slip": (H, W) 8 方向の ρ の最大, "alpha", "cell"}. Cross slope (rollover, side slip) is not included.
